subject: pe
title: Physical Activity Project and Performance Assessment
keyDates: September 2026 — teacher tells the SEC which activity each student will use for the Performance Assessment (prescribed date in September of sixth year per the 2018 guidelines; exact 2027 date TBC by SEC)
Early October to mid-December 2026 — Physical Activity Project window (8 to 10 weeks, about 20 to 25 hours; 2018-spec guidelines)
October 2026 and January 2027 — check examinations.ie for PAP guidelines/booklet (OIDE advice)
Mid-December 2026 — PAP completion date; 2027 exact date TBC by SEC circular (for comparison, 2026 cycle was 12 December 2025 completion, school upload 12-15 January 2026)
January to March 2027 — Performance Assessment filmed in PE class (2018 guidelines)
Late March 2027 — Performance Assessment completion date; exact 2027 date TBC by SEC circular (2026 cycle: 23 March completion, upload 24-27 March)
June 2027 — 2.5-hour written exam (50%); last year of the 2018 specification, the redeveloped spec is first examined June 2028
summary: Physical Education has three parts: a 50% written exam, a 20% Physical Activity Project (PAP, Higher and Ordinary level) and a 30% Performance Assessment (common level). In the PAP you pick a competitive sport and a role (performer or coach/choreographer), analyse your performance, set goals, train, retest and reflect, then submit a word-limited PDF booklet with short MP4 videos. In the Performance Assessment you submit one video of yourself performing in one of your three studied activities, in a different activity area from the PAP.

stages.name: PAP: Choose activity and role
stages.marksNote: Not marked directly, but an invalid choice puts the whole PAP at risk.

points: The activity must be a competitive sport with a national governing body affiliated to Sport Ireland, and fit the Irish Sports Council Act 1999 definition of competitive sport (organised participation aiming at improved results in competition).

Check validity three ways: the physical activity areas page of the specification, the Sport Ireland NGB finder, then the SEC (schoolsportal@examinations.ie) if still unsure. Your teacher authenticates the choice.
Affiliated but non-competitive (e.g. angling) or competitive but unaffiliated (e.g. powerlifting) are given by OIDE as invalid examples.
Do the PAP on the activity as a whole, not a single skill or exercise.
Your school makes the final decision on which activities it can support, especially outside school.
The PAP activity must be in a different physical activity area from your Performance Assessment activity. Hurling and soccer are both Games, so you could not use one for each.
Golf, triathlon or boxing may be allowed for the PAP even if not listed in the specification, but cannot be used for the Performance Assessment, which needs a specified activity.
A Studyclix teacher guide advises deciding your Performance Assessment activity first and saving your strongest sport for it, because that is where you are graded on skill.
Performer: you analyse and improve your own performance.
Coach/choreographer: you analyse and lead a peer (a senior-cycle student) through the plan. Parental consent for the peer is required.
Both roles follow the same project structure.
A PE teacher or another registered teacher on the school staff must accompany you when filming outside school, and a representative of the club must be present.
Sign the school consent forms; the club's image rules cannot be overridden by consent forms.
Keep the number of other people on camera to a minimum.

checklistCandidates: Confirm your sport has a Sport Ireland-affiliated NGB and is competitive
Pick a PAP activity from a different activity area to your Performance Assessment
Get your teacher to confirm the activity and role before you start

stages.name: PAP: Section A - needs analysis and performance analysis
stages.marksNote: Section A, about 700 words; marks reported as 25 by a PEAI teacher presentation (a Studyclix guide gives 12 - see conflicts).

points: List what the activity demands across the areas in the guidelines: skill and technique, psychological demands, physiological demands, performance-related fitness, health-related fitness, biomechanical/movement analysis, structures and strategies, roles and relationships, diet and nutrition.
Keep a source log as you research, because you must reference everything and list sources in the bibliography.
Design a test battery from your needs analysis and run it in class under teacher supervision.
Compare every result with normative data in a table, and cite where the norms came from.
Also collect model-performer comparison, stage of learning, tactics, psychological (e.g. SCAT) and match or observation sheets where relevant.
Everyone in the class doing all the tests makes administration easier (teacher advice).
Include a brief personal introduction, your exam number, why you chose the activity, your skill level, and key findings with references.
Label every figure (Fig.1 etc.) and refer to it in the text; images must not be used to smuggle in extra text.
Interpret results; do not just describe them. The descriptors separate analytical from merely descriptive work.
Keep your data relevant to the goals you will set in Section B.
Your video must show you engaging in the activity (for example video analysis that adds to, not repeats, the written text).
Short snippets of each test (10-20 seconds) are enough; Studyclix suggests about a minute in total.
No slides of text, images or audio reflections as part of videos, and no video collages except a two-video side-by-side skill comparison (OIDE, 2025 booklet).

checklistCandidates: Test every component relevant to your activity and compare with cited normative data
Label each figure and refer to it in the text
Interpret what the results mean for performance rather than describing them
Film short test clips that show you doing the activity

stages.name: PAP: Section B - performance goals and training plans
stages.marksNote: Section B, about 400-450 words; 40 marks per a PEAI teacher presentation and a Studyclix guide.

points: Set distinct goals, one per area (skill and technique, psychological, physiological, performance-related fitness, health-related fitness, biomechanical, structures/strategies, roles and relationships, diet and nutrition). Agility and coordination are both performance-related fitness, so only one of them counts.
The official 2019 guidelines say four goals; the 2025/26 teacher guidance found says three - confirm with your SEC booklet (see conflicts).
Every goal must come from evidence in Section A.

Write each goal as SMART (specific, measurable, achievable, relevant/realistic, time-bound), with a baseline, a target, a time frame and the test used. Example from OIDE: 20m shuttle run from 9.4 to 10.2 shuttles over five weeks.
Give a short rationale for each goal linked to the Section A result.
Write a separate training plan per goal in the booklet's table, usually 4-6 weeks (Studyclix), so someone else could follow it.
Justify methods with principles of training and theory.
Bring in a distinct approach per goal rather than three similar fitness plans.
Film real engagement in your plans; at least two samples of the same exercise at different points show progress.
Section B video must show authentic engagement, not staged clips.
Keep a note of each session and what you changed, because Section C asks how you responded to challenges.

checklistCandidates: Write each goal as SMART with baseline, target and deadline
Make every goal distinct and traceable to Section A data
Write one separate, followable training plan per goal
Justify each plan with principles of training
Film real, repeated engagement in the plans

stages.name: PAP: Section C - retest and concluding analysis
stages.marksNote: Section C, about 450-500 words; 25 marks per PEAI and Studyclix.

points: Repeat all Section A tests, not only those tied to your goals, under the same conditions.
Reuse the Section A table so comparisons are direct, referring back to the same figures.
State for each goal whether it was achieved, with the numbers, and why or why not.
Discuss unintended outcomes: improvements or changes in other tests caused by your training.
Evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of each plan and how you responded to challenges.
Give realistic next steps for each goal.
Link back to theory; the top descriptor needs an in-depth understanding of the factors affecting performance.
Show a short clip of each retest and engagement in the activity, complementing rather than repeating the text.
Total of all three videos is capped at 4 minutes (OIDE, 2025 booklet).

checklistCandidates: Retest everything you tested in Section A
State achieved or not for each goal with numbers and a reason
Identify unintended outcomes
Evaluate each plan and give realistic next steps

stages.name: PAP: Formatting, coherence and submission
stages.marksNote: Overall coherence and references, 10 marks per PEAI and Studyclix; penalties apply for breaking format rules.

points: Total 1,600 words across Sections A to C, excluding references and bibliography; OIDE lists about 700/450/450, Studyclix and PEAI about 700/400/500.
Arial 12; bullets, bold and italics allowed.
The booklet must be a PDF before submission; schools upload four files: PDF, Section A MP4, Section B MP4, Section C MP4.
Videos total a maximum of 4 minutes combined, in MP4.
Use brackets for in-text sources, e.g. (topendsports.com), and put full details in the bibliography so links do not cost words.
Each candidate submits a separate, distinct PAP, even when working with classmates.
Section B must build on A, and C on A and B.
Videos should add clarity and support the text in all three sections.
Avoid repetition and waffle.
Proofread the printed PDF: anything not visible cannot earn marks.
You sign a P.2 form confirming that the printed PDF matches the submitted version.

checklistCandidates: Stay within 1,600 words, Arial 12
Keep the three videos under 4 minutes combined, MP4, no text slides
Link Section A, B and C
Reference every source and add a bibliography
Print and proofread the final PDF before signing P.2

stages.name: Performance: Choose activity and plan
stages.marksNote: Performance Assessment, 30% of LCPE, common level.

points: Pick one of the three activities you studied, agreed with your teacher; it must be from a different activity area to your PAP.
Your teacher notifies the SEC of the activity in September of sixth year.

Options: Games, Aquatics, Adventure activities, Athletics, Artistic and aesthetic movement, or Personal exercise and fitness (NCCA noted a proposal to remove this last option for the new specification only).

guide.h: What the video must show, by scenario
points: Games, Aquatics, Adventure, Athletics: skills and techniques from the specification, tactics and/or strategies, and awareness of safety, equipment and rules, in a mix of contexts such as fully competitive, conditioned practices, individual and group.

Artistic and aesthetic: imaginative combinations of skills (gymnastics) or movements (dance), compositional/choreographic design including props or costume, creativity, and safety, in two of individual, pair, group.

Personal exercise and fitness: a personal programme to improve either performance-related or health-related fitness, with one aerobic method and one conditioning/resistance method, each applying principles of training, training zones, thresholds, work-recovery intervals and warm-up/cool-down.
In every case you introduce the video by stating the performance characteristics you want examiners to notice.

checklistCandidates: Choose an activity from a different area to your PAP
Plan to show performance in more than one context
Prepare a short introduction naming what to look for

stages.name: Performance: Film and submit
stages.marksNote: Marked against the quality descriptors for your activity area; the SEC marks from your video.

points: Filming is done in PE class under teacher supervision between January and March of sixth year, about 10 hours of work.
Capture, editing and publishing are done in school under teacher monitoring for authentication.
Be clearly identifiable in group play, for example with a bib.
You should be the main, clearly visible subject; keep other people on camera to a minimum.
Upload footage to the school's secure storage quickly and delete it from the device after backup.
One MP4 video is submitted (file named with year, subject code 225, component 3 and your exam number).
A teacher guide (Folens/ABC) and an OIDE slide give a maximum of 8 minutes and up to 6 text frames, with material beyond that not marked; this is secondary, so verify against the SEC brief.
Games: wide range of skills, using both dominant and non-dominant sides, success under pressure, creativity in different contexts, tactical knowledge, rules and safety.

Aquatics, Adventure, Athletics: very high accuracy, control and fluency, success under pressure or in challenging situations, strong tactical knowledge/decision-making, comprehensive rules and safety.
Artistic: extensive repertoire, proficiency and fluency, creativity, prominent compositional knowledge, safety.

checklistCandidates: Film in class under teacher supervision, January to March
Make yourself identifiable in group scenes
Show wide skill range, tactics, rules and safety in different contexts
Keep within the SEC length limit and MP4 format

criteria.name: PAP Section A: Performance analysis
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: A variety of comprehensive self-analysis tools, interpreted analytically across all areas of the specification, with data compared with normative data and referenced. Mark figure from PEAI teacher presentation; Studyclix shows 12.

criteria.name: PAP Section B: Performance goals, plans and implementation
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: Distinct, pertinent, SMART goals drawn from Section A with detailed corrective measures grounded in theory, a followable plan per goal, and detailed evidence of real implementation.

criteria.name: PAP Section C: Concluding analysis
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: Retest of all Section A tests, in-depth theoretical understanding, excellent analysis of progress per goal, strengths and weaknesses of the programme, unintended outcomes and constructive next steps.

criteria.name: PAP overall coherence and references
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: Sections link logically, videos support the text, correct word count, font, video length, labelling and full referencing.

criteria.name: Performance Assessment (whole video)
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: Extensive repertoire executed with high accuracy, control and fluency, success in varied or pressured contexts, tactical or compositional knowledge, rules knowledge and high adherence to safety. Mark total not found in sources.

rules: The PAP must be in a competitive sport with a Sport Ireland-affiliated NGB.
PAP and Performance Assessment activities must be in different physical activity areas.
The PAP is your own work, completed in PE class under teacher supervision; you may train with peers but must submit individual reports based on your own goals.
Editing and publishing of videos is done in school under teacher monitoring.
Booklet limit of 1,600 words excluding references; Arial 12; PDF format.
PAP videos total no more than 4 minutes, MP4, with no text slides, audio reflections or collages (side-by-side skill comparison allowed).
Images must not carry additional text.
Anyone filmed has signed consent; out-of-school filming needs a teacher and a club representative present.
Filenames must follow the SEC naming convention or the Schools Portal rejects them.
You sign P.2 confirming the printed PDF matches the submission.
Missing a deadline needs an SEC-approved extension; the portal re-opens only for those cases.
mistakes: Choosing a PAP activity in the same activity area as the Performance Assessment.
Choosing a sport that is not a competitive sport with an affiliated NGB.
Doing a single skill or exercise instead of the activity as a whole.
Goals from the same area (e.g. agility and coordination both performance-related fitness).
Goals without Section A evidence behind them.
Describing results instead of interpreting them.
Retesting only the goal-related tests in Section C.
Putting text in images or video slides, or leaving audio on without need (Studyclix says videos with sound lose marks - unverified).
Going over the word or video limits, or not proofreading the printed PDF.
Filming without being identifiable in group play for the Performance Assessment.

conflicts: Number of PAP goals: the 2019 guidelines and the app say four; the 2025/26 Studyclix teacher guide says three goals and three training plans, and OIDE slides refer to 'training plans' without a count. The SEC's current booklet decides; confirm with your teacher.

Section marks: PEAI presentation gives A 25, B 40, C 25, coherence 10 (total 100); Studyclix lists A as 12, which does not sum to 100. No official mark breakdown was reachable, so treat 25/40/25/10 as likely.
Word split: OIDE says B 450 and C 450, while Studyclix and PEAI say B 400 and C 500; the total (1,600) and A (700) agree.

The app's PAP note describes a four-section cycle with ongoing reflection, and its planning note suggests monitoring logs and mid-programme retests. The current booklet has A, B and C only, with reflection folded into B/C; no standalone ongoing-reflection section is marked.

The 2019 guidelines require four short reflections (one per goal) in the ongoing training section; the current three-section booklet has no such section. This is the main source of difference with the app.
Performance Assessment video length (8 minutes) comes from secondary sources only.

The app says the Performance Assessment is 30% at common level, which agrees with sources. A search result said the PE project is 50% under the new specification; this applies only to students starting in 2026 and not the June 2027 cohort.
Exact 2027 dates have not been published in the sources found; dates above are patterns from 2026 and the 2018 guidelines.
2018 and 2019 guidelines are older than the SEC booklets; where the two differ, the booklet governs.
